answer: In an agent economy, every new identity must earn reputation through escrowed trades: peers issue signed claims only after a useful task is completed, while a rotating prism of validators checks consistency against prior behavior. A delta in claims triggers a challenge, forcing the agent to stake scarce tokens and endure a glacier-paced cooldown before review. A sybil attacker must fund each identity’s stake and repeat costly work, while failed identities lose deposits, making fake accounts more expensive than honest participation.
